doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

title: About two years at the Rialto and the history of Luchenbach's
summary: Billie stayed two years at the Rialto, then describes Luchenbach's old folks home restaurant and dance hall.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: He must've worked with some good bands. Ah, man. Well, I don't think he worked with too many bands. Well, of course, what I mean, because I know that when he worked with Santa, they stayed on that boat that's so long, you know. I don't think that he worked around with too many bands. So, after they sold that boat, Ruby just give up all the music altogether and went with the Southern Riemont, you see? And he's still with them. Yes. Yes. That's what we're killing. So, how long did you stay with Piku? I stayed with Piku. Oh, I stayed with Piku. I stayed with Piku, I guess around about... I'm going to stay with Piku about a couple of years. About a couple of years, we held that job down in Rialto. Did you play any other places? No, I didn't have no other places. I couldn't play no other places because I was waking every night.
Yeah, but I mean, that band stayed the entire two years at the Rialto. Yeah. Rialto.

And then what happened? Then, uh, after I left the Rialto, I started with, you know, after I left the Rialto, I think I must have went to Lutches. What's Lutches? Bill Paul down there, old folks home. That's Lutches. Yeah. Yeah. What goes on there? You ain't never been that old folks home, Dick. No. You're a little chug. You can't tell me. I know Dick killed me. I know Dick killed me. I was a monster and beret. Yeah. Yeah. I stayed there, huh? No, but what was it then when you first went there? Same thing it is now. Same thing. Exactly. It hadn't changed a bit. It didn't change a bit.

What was it before you went in? Oh, it was a restaurant and bar. Used to have seafood, you know, thing like that. And the bar and port. And, uh, where the dance division is now, that was open. That was open between there and the house in the back, which is the home. They lived there and they had empty light in between. They closed the lot and built a dance hall.
